title: Trade licence renewal in the UAE: costs and deadlines
summary: Planning a Dubai trade licence renewal? Learn what renewal costs include, which documents you need, when to start, what happens after expiry, and how renewal differs across UAE emirates.
body_markdown:
## What does trade licence renewal involve?


If you renew a UAE trade licence every year, the process is familiar. The problem usually starts when the expiry date arrives before the paperwork does.


Your first step is identifying the authority that issued the licence. Dubai mainland businesses generally renew through Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, while free zone businesses use their relevant free zone authority.


For Dubai mainland businesses, you can start with the official[Dubai trade licence renewal service](https://app.invest.dubai.ae/license/renew/email) . Other emirates have their own portals and requirements.


The process usually involves checking the licence details, confirming required documents or approvals, paying the applicable fees, and receiving the renewed licence.


The exact requirements depend on the licence, activity, emirate, and issuing authority.


## How much does trade licence renewal cost?


There is no single UAE trade licence renewal fee.


For Dubai, the amount depends on the applicable licensing tariff and the details of your business. That means a headline figure found online may not be your final bill.


When budgeting for renewal, check:


Cost What to check


Licence renewal Applicable fee for your licence and activities


Activity charges Additional fees for specific activities


Tenancy costs Lease, Ejari, or related renewal costs


Registrations Commercial register or other applicable registrations


External approvals Required for certain regulated activities


Late fees Applicable if renewal happens after expiry


For example, Dubai Development Authority states that commercial licence renewal fees are charged according to its tariff, with an additional AED 10 Knowledge Dirham and AED 10 Innovation Dirham per transaction. Its service is available online 24/7.


Ajman's official renewal service gives a clearer example of how several charges can sit behind the headline fee. It lists AED 600 for economic licence renewal, AED 50 for the administrative services application, AED 200 for commercial register registration, and AED 200 for registration in the unified economic activities register, with other charges applying in specific cases.


Ajman also provides an online[licence fee calculator](https://eservices.ajmanded.ae/en/calcLicensefees) , where businesses enter details such as the existing licence, legal form, activity, investor count, and licence number.


For more detail on Dubai costs, see our guide to[trade licence costs in Dubai](https://www.alaan.com/blog/dubai-trade-licence-cost-requirements-guide) .


## What do you need before starting?


Requirements vary, but check these before opening the renewal application:


- Current trade licence details
- Valid tenancy or lease documents
- Ejari or equivalent registration, where applicable
- External approvals for regulated activities
- Company documents requested by the authority
- Outstanding fees or penalties


Tenancy is an easy one to overlook. Ajman's official renewal process, for example, starts with lease-contract certification and may require external approvals depending on the business activity.


Check these documents early rather than discovering a problem when the licence is about to expire.


## When should you renew?


Start reviewing the renewal at least 30 days before expiry. This is a practical planning recommendation, not a universal UAE deadline.


The actual renewal rules depend on the issuing authority and licence type.


For example, Dubai Development Authority advises free zone licence holders to renew their trade licence on time annually and maintain a valid licence. Its commercial licence renewal service is available online 24/7 and lists an estimated immediate delivery time once the requirements are completed.


So, rather than waiting for the expiry date, work backwards from it. Give yourself enough time to fix a tenancy issue, obtain an approval, or resolve an outstanding payment if something gets stuck.


## What happens if your licence lapses?


The consequences depend on the authority, licence type, and length of the delay.


A business may face:


- Late-renewal fees or penalties
- Additional administrative charges
- Restrictions on certain government transactions
- Problems with related business or immigration services
- Extra work if the licence remains expired


There is no single UAE-wide grace period that you should apply to every trade licence.


Ajman's official service specifically refers to one month after licence expiry and states that late renewal fees can apply after the permitted period.


That does not mean the same rule applies to a Dubai mainland licence or every free zone. Check the rules attached to your own licence before assuming you have a particular grace period.


## How does renewal differ across UAE emirates?


The mainland/free zone distinction matters here. A Dubai free zone licence is not renewed through the same process as a Dubai mainland licence.


For example, Dubai Development Authority has its own online commercial licence renewal service for businesses in its free zone.


If you operate from a free zone, start with the authority named on your licence.


Emirate Renewal route What to watch


Dubai DET/Invest in Dubai for mainland licences; relevant free zone for free zone licences Fees depend on the licence and applicable tariff


Abu Dhabi Abu Dhabi DED through TAMM Use the current economic licence renewal service and licence-specific requirements


Sharjah Sharjah Economic Development Department or relevant free zone Mainland and free zone processes differ


Ajman Ajman DED eServices Lease certification and applicable registrations may form part of renewal


## How to keep renewal off the to-do list


Treat licence renewal as a recurring finance commitment, not an annual surprise.


Add the expiry date to your[payment calendar](https://www.alaan.com/payment-calendar) and set reminders for:


1. 60 days before: check the licence, lease, and required documents.
2. 30 days before: confirm the renewal cost and start the application.
3. After renewal: save the renewed licence, receipt, and next expiry date.


An[expense management platform](https://www.alaan.com/services/expense-management-platform) can also help finance teams keep recurring business expenses organised alongside other payments.


The point is simple: the licence may renew once a year, but the finance team should not have to remember it once a year.


## FAQs


### How do I renew my UAE trade licence?


Use the renewal portal of the authority that issued your licence. Dubai mainland businesses can use the official[Invest in Dubai renewal service](https://app.invest.dubai.ae/license/renew/email) . Free zone businesses should use their relevant free zone portal.


### How much is trade licence renewal in the UAE?


There is no single UAE-wide fee. The cost depends on the emirate, authority, licence type, activities, registrations, and other applicable charges.


### How many days does trade licence renewal take?


Processing time varies. Some authorities provide immediate online processing when requirements are complete. Dubai Development Authority, for example, lists immediate delivery for its commercial licence renewal service.


### Does Dubai have a grace period for trade licence renewal?


Do not assume a universal grace period. Rules vary by licensing authority and licence type. Check the current requirements for your specific licence.


### Can I renew my trade licence online?


Yes, many UAE authorities provide online renewal. Dubai, Ajman, and the Dubai Development Authority all provide online renewal services.
